name: Grand Duchy of Berg
alt: Grand Duchy of Cleves and Berg
Grand Duchy of Berg and Cleves

predecessors.name: Duchy of Jülich-Berg
predecessors.text: the Duchy of Berg, ceded by Maximilian I Joseph of Bavaria to Napoleon on 15 March 1806 (de page)

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Prussia
predecessors.text: Wesel and the right bank of the former Duchy of Cleves

successors.name: Kingdom of Prussia
successors.text: no Berg shape exists after November 1813; the land of the former grand duchy, administered as the Generalgouvernement Berg until Prussia and Hanover took it by the Final Act of the Congress of Vienna

ledger.x: 15 March 1806: Napoleon puts the Duchy of Berg under Joachim Murat.
March 1806: Cleves east of the Rhine joins Berg.
1806: the Nassau-Orange principalities of Siegen, Dillenburg and Hadamar join Berg in the south, with the Rhine Confederation Act (12 July 1806, CoR page; 'Mit Wirkung vom 1.
1806: the Rhine Confederation Act adds mediatised lands.
1807: after the Peace of Tilsit Berg receives Prussian lands.
13 December 1810: France annexes the northern Berg lands.
November 1813: after Leipzig the grand duchy collapses.

wars.name: War of the Fourth Coalition
wars.outcome: Prussia defeated at Jena and Auerstedt (14 October 1806) and by the Treaty of Tilsit of 9 July 1807, which 'stripped the country of about half its territory'; the Prussian lands Mark, Münster, Essen, Werden, Lingen, Tecklenburg and Cleves east of the Rhine…

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition
wars.outcome: The Battle of Leipzig (19 October 1813) breaks the Confederation of the Rhine, dissolved on 4 November 1813; Allied troops enter Düsseldorf on 10 November (de page) and Berg ends.

certainty.note: The state was assembled piecemeal from mediatised lands and Prussian cessions; the page says the north-eastern lands lay cut off from the rest of the state and were reachable only through Salm.
Four departments, 12 arrondissements and 78 cantons were fixed by the Burgos decree of 14 November 1808; the 1810 cut follows a line from the Lippe via Haltern and Telgte to Borgholzhausen.
